subject: Science
title: Our science celebration
objectives: Children will show Year learning through games and a science fair.
Teachers will complete every child’s end-of-year record and transition note.
content: Revising the body, senses and materials, living things, and celebrating the year with end-of-year records and a transition note.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly; record what children can do; invite parents to the celebration; complete the transition note honestly for the next teacher.
learnerActivities: Show what they know through games and a small science fair and enjoy a celebration.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s end-of-year science learning and complete the transition note.
expectedOutcomes: Takes part confidently in familiar science games.
Each child has an end-of-year observation record.

lessons.title: Revising body, senses and materials
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit the body, senses, water, sand, soil and materials through games.
successCriteria: Uses words such as wet, dry, float and sink
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about the body, senses, materials, living things, movement, light and caring this year.
resources: A water basin with float and sink objects
lessons.starter: Sing the body song and say "Today we play our favourite body, senses and materials games."
teacherActivities: Play the mystery bag game with touch.
Play float and sink with the basin.
Sort objects into natural and made.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
learnerActivities: Child puts an object in the water and says float or sink.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the mystery bag game with touch. Children: Child feels and guesses.
Step 2. Teacher: Play float and sink with the basin. Children: Child puts an object in the water and says float or sink.
Step 3. Teacher: Sort objects into natural and made. Children: Child sorts the objects.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Body and materials games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
The teacher notes which words each child uses.
practical.safety: Keep water shallow and the floor clear. Supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use two objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Shows knowledge of body, senses and materials
lessons.homeConnection: Play body and materials games at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit the body, senses, water, sand, soil and materials through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Revising living things
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will revisit animals, plants, seeds and caring for living things.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about the body, senses, materials, living things, movement, light and caring this year.
lessons.starter: Look at our plants and say "Our plants have grown. Let us look after them."
teacherActivities: Match animals to homes and babies to mothers.
Look at the grown plants and name the parts.
Sort foods into plant and animal foods.
learnerActivities: Child names a leaf or flower.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Match animals to homes and babies to mothers. Children: Child matches the cards.
Step 2. Teacher: Look at the grown plants and name the parts. Children: Child names a leaf or flower.
Step 3. Teacher: Water the plants together. Children: Child waters a plant.
Step 4. Teacher: Sort foods into plant and animal foods. Children: Child sorts food pictures.

practical.title: Living things games
steps: The teacher notes names and care.
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Wash hands after touching plants.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and name each item.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to explain how to care for a plant.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "We care for living things."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep caring for plants and animals at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit animals, plants, seeds and caring for living things" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Science fair stations
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year science learning at a small science fair.
successCriteria: Shows body, senses, living things, movement and light knowledge
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about the body, senses, materials, living things, movement, light and caring this year.
lessons.starter: Say "Today is our science fair. We visit six stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: senses, float and sink, plants, push and pull, shadows and caring.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: senses, float and sink, plants, push and pull, shadows and caring. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they can do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Science fair
steps: Set up six stations with familiar materials.
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep water shallow, torches covered and floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: uses senses; says float or sink; names plants and animals; pushes and pulls; makes a shadow; cares for living things.

lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite science game at home during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s end-of-year science learning at a small science fair" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Science celebration
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will celebrate the year with songs, experiments and plants, and show their work to visitors.
successCriteria: Shows something they enjoyed to an adult
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about the body, senses, materials, living things, movement, light and caring this year.
resources: The grown plants and children’s work
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate everything we discovered. Let us sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions.
Invite children to show their plants or work to a visitor or parent.
Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Invite children to show their plants or work to a visitor or parent. Children: Child shows their work.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a sticker or certificate and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.

practical.title: Celebration circle
steps: Sit in a circle with visitors.
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Supervise visitors and keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and share their work together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s end-of-year science record from the year’s observations. Record the child’s strengths and a next step for Nursery 1.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you in Nursery 1."
lessons.homeConnection: Keep exploring, asking questions and looking at nature during the holiday.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "celebrate the year with songs, experiments and plants, and show their work to visitors" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Transition note and records
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will complete a transition note for each child for the Nursery 1 teacher.
successCriteria: Records what each child can do
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about the body, senses, materials, living things, movement, light and caring this year.
lessons.starter: Today the children enjoy free play with familiar materials while the teacher completes the transition notes.
teacherActivities: Set out free play with sand, water, plants and puzzles.
Review each child’s three term records and portfolio.
Complete the note: strengths, interests, language, science skills and next steps.
learnerActivities: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Children play and talk with the helper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set out free play with sand, water, plants and puzzles. Children: Children play freely and happily.
Step 2. Teacher: Review each child’s three term records and portfolio. Children: Children play while the teacher reviews.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete the note: strengths, interests, language, science skills and next steps. Children: Children play and talk with the helper.

practical.title: Free play and records
steps: Set out four play areas with a helper.
The teacher reviews records at a quiet table.
The teacher completes each transition note.
practical.safety: A second adult must supervise play while the teacher completes the notes. Keep water shallow and all areas safe and tidy.

differentiation.support: Offer familiar toys and a helper nearby.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to help a friend tidy up.

assessment.method: Write for each child: what they can do in using the senses, exploring materials, knowing plants and animals, movement and caring; their interests; any support needed; and a next step. Use the four-level scale and facts you have seen.

questions.question: What do you like to play?
What did you discover this year?

expectedOutcomes: Has a transition note for each child
lessons.conclusion: Tidy up together and say goodbye to the year.
lessons.homeConnection: Share the end-of-year report with your child and keep exploring together.

What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
